docs.title: mobileAX
docs.text:
A millisecond-latency CLI for driving Android devices. Built for LLM agents and shell scripts.

mobileAX is the smallest thing that gives you a tap, a type, and a wait on a real Android device, from any language. It is one Rust CLI on the host and one small jar on the device — no installed app, no root, no WebDriver server. A single call costs a few milliseconds.

This guide reads as a story. Start at the top.

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
The standard ways to drive an Android device are heavy. adb shell input tap X Y works for coordinates but can't find a button by label. uiautomator2 makes you install two APKs and speaks only Python. Appium asks you to bring up a WebDriver server and then pays ~100 ms per click on top of that. None of these were designed for the case that's most common today: an LLM loop or a shell script that wants to call tap("Continue") thousands of times in an afternoon.

mobileAX is designed exactly for that loop. You drop one jar on the device, the daemon stays warm under app_process, and the CLI talks to it over a length-prefixed binary protocol. A round trip is 2–7 ms. Every action verb returns a structured exit code so unattended scripts can branch without parsing stderr.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
You need adb on $PATH (brew install android-platform-tools on macOS, the matching android-tools package on Linux). Then:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pbk20191/mobileax/main/install.sh | bash

USB debugging on, plug the phone in, confirm adb devices lists it, and you're ready.

docs.title: The agent loop
docs.text:
This is the one passage to read if you read nothing else.

mobax use                 # auto-detect a device, start the daemon
mobax ui                  # flat table of tappable nodes — drop into an LLM
mobax tap "Continue"      # the LLM picks a label, you tap it
mobax wait "Welcome"      # block on the next screen
mobax drop                # tear it all down

mobax ui (since v0.1.14 the interactive table is the default) returns one line per actionable node:

fill  EditText  "Email"     #email     540,540
fill  EditText  "Password"  #password  540,640  [password]
tap   Button    "Continue"  #continue  540,860

Hand that to a model, get back a label, hand the label to mobax tap. That's the loop. The full XML hierarchy is still one flag away (mobax ui --xml), but for an LLM the flat table is roughly 10× cheaper in tokens.

docs.title: Selectors
docs.text:
When labels collide or you need a more specific match, mobax find and the selector-aware verbs accept a CSS-like grammar. The vocabulary is borrowed from Playwright's locator API on purpose, so muscle memory transfers.

mobax tap 'Button[text="Sign in"]'                   # exact text
mobax tap 'Button:has-text("Sign in")'               # substring (Playwright sugar)
mobax tap 'EditText:below(TextView[text=Email])'     # relational
mobax tap 'Button:near(ImageView[desc~=cart], 200)'  # within 200 px
mobax tap '[role=Switch][state=Off]'                 # Compose role / state

Compose and androidx widgets expose a role and a state (in the device's language: 스위치 / 사용 안함 on a Korean device), and mobax ui shows them next to each row. The full set of pseudo-classes (:visible, :clickable, :editable, :heading, :in(), :below(), :right-of(), :near(), :has-text(), :text-is()) is documented in the cookbook.

docs.title: Reliability
docs.text:
Every action verb honours the same set of flags so RPA scripts stop hand-rolling retry loops:

mobax tap "Refresh" --visible --unique --timeout 3s --retries 4 --retry-delay 500ms

Failures funnel through structured exit codes:

Code Meaning 0 ok 1 failure (everything below not broken out — full code in error.code when --json) 2 NOT_FOUND 3 TIMEOUT 4 AMBIGUOUS — --unique saw more than one match

That deliberate small alphabet is the thing scripts actually branch on. The full structured ErrCode lives in JSON-mode output for any caller that wants to dispatch on the long tail (DAEMON_ERROR, SECURE_WINDOW, BAD_ARG, etc.).

docs.title: JSON output and language bindings
docs.text:
--json (or HS_FORMAT=json) makes every action verb emit one structured line:

{"verb":"tap","ok":true,"result":{"x":540,"y":860,"text":"Continue"}}
{"verb":"tap","ok":false,"error":{"code":"NOT_FOUND","detail":"no node matched"}}

That's the shape any subprocess driver should consume. A first-party Python SDK lives under bindings/python/; other languages can drive the CLI in ~30 lines of subprocess code.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
host                                  device (shell UID, app_process)
─────                                  ──────────────────────────────
mobax <verb> ──► adb server ─────►     MobaxServer → Dispatch (one coroutine per connection)
                                       ├─ Server.respond     sync verbs (Pm Am Wm Props Providers …)
                                       ├─ Gestures           input, wait_for_*, tap_and_*
                                       ├─ Transfers          push/pull, install, uninstall
                                       ├─ ProcStream         dumpsys logcat shell monitor clip_watch
                                       ├─ Streams            stream, stream_tilejpeg, stream_h264
                                       ├─ State + StateRefresher  (push-cached snapshot, state_watch)
                                       └─ UiEvents / Waits   (accessibility event fan-out)

The daemon runs as the shell UID via app_process with hidden-API restrictions lifted. It listens on the abstract Unix socket @mobaxd_<port> (the host opens it through the adb server: host:transport:SERIAL, then localabstract:mobaxd_<port>, with no host port forward) and refuses any peer whose SO_PEERCRED uid isn't shell or root. The host runs a background state-daemon that subscribes to state_watch and atomically rewrites ~/.mobileax/state-<port>.json on every event-driven refresh. mobax info / mobax info / mobax show all read straight out of that file.

docs.title: Threads
docs.text:
One main thread runs Looper.loop(). Sockets, process pipes and the dumpsys pipe are registered with the main MessageQueue (epoll) through Io; each connection is a Conn driven by a coroutine on Dispatchers.Main. Accessibility events, display/package/config listeners, ImageReader and MediaCodec callbacks, and all timers (delay) run there too. Nothing on the main thread may block.

Everything off main runs on the kotlinx-coroutines scheduler, so all of it shares one worker pool (DefaultDispatcher-worker-N):

  • Loop.Work (Default.limitedParallelism(≤4)): CPU work and binder calls that can take long — JPEG/PNG encoding, tile diffs, accessibility tree dumps, PackageInstaller and file I/O.
  • Loop.Blocking (IO): calls that wait on a peer — binder dumps into a pipe a slow client drains, MediaCodec / VirtualDisplay setup and teardown.
  • Loop.FrameCopy (IO.limitedParallelism(1)): mirror pixel copies, which block on the GPU fence once per frame.

Gestures pace MOVE events on Choreographer vsync callbacks; stream fps=N sends on the first vsync after each slot. state_watch and clip_watch collect StateFlows (one clipboard poller per interval, only while watched).

Output is queued per connection: send applies backpressure past 4 MiB; sendLatest keeps only the newest unsent frame (JPEG stream, state_watch). stream_h264 connections with the same parameters share one encoder; each access unit is copied once. Joiners and lagging viewers restart from cached SPS/PPS + the frames since the last IDR, so the shared encoder never waits.

wire-smoke.py run / diff (in scripts/) records normalized responses for every verb so two daemon builds can be compared on a device.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
src/dev/mobileax/daemon/      on-device daemon (Kotlin → dex → jar)
mobax-cli/                 host CLI — short-verb surface (`mobax use`, `mobax see`, …)
mobax-viewer/              GUI mirror — winit + GPU decode (Metal/VideoToolbox, D3D11/MF, GLES/VA-API)
build.gradle.kts              AGP: kotlinc → R8 → unsigned APK → build/mobax.jar  (build.sh wraps it)

docs.title: Benchmark
docs.text:
Measured on 2026-05-24 with n=50 on the Android 15 emulator Google sdk_gphone64_arm64 (1440x3120, SDK 35), host macOS/aarch64. Numbers are p50 with p95 in parentheses. mobax uses one warm daemon socket; adb starts a fresh adb CLI process per sample.

Reproduce the mobileAX side with mobax bench -n 50 or machine-readable mobax bench -n 50 --json. Reproduce raw ADB baselines with scripts/bench-adb.sh -n 50; the script keeps the exact ADB commands inspectable.

The default mobax bench suite follows the hot path: 768px JPEG screenshots for agents, with WebP as a lossy export comparison. PNG is intentionally left out of the headline mobax suite because Android's PNG encoder is a debug/export path, not an interaction loop path.

docs.title: Cookbook
docs.text:
Recipes for driving Android with mobax. Each one is copy-pasteable into a real terminal.

These build on the agent loop in the README and the verb table in mobax --help. If you've never run mobax use, start there. The shared action flags (--timeout, --retries, --visible, --unique, --nth, --json, …) work on every action verb; this page shows them in context rather than restating the table.

docs.title: Fast agent loop
docs.text:
Use the UI table as the primary model input. It is small, text-first, and already contains the center coordinates mobileAX will tap.

mobax use
mobax ui > /tmp/mobax-screen.txt

Only add an image when the visual layout matters. Keep it agent-sized:

mobax see --size 768 /tmp/mobax-screen.jpg

mobax see out.jpg without --size is a native-resolution export for bug reports and pixel debugging. It is slower and much larger than the 768px agent path. PNG is lossless/debug only:

mobax see --native /tmp/full.jpg
mobax see --native /tmp/full.png

docs.title: Logging in
docs.text:
The canonical flow: find the email field, fill it, find the password field, fill it, submit, and wait for the dashboard.

mobax use
mobax wait idle 200ms

mobax tap   "Sign in"              --visible --unique --timeout 5s
mobax fill  '#email'                'you@example.com'   # same as [id=email]
mobax fill  'EditText[resource-id=com.example:id/password]' "hunter2"
mobax submit
mobax wait  "Dashboard"            --timeout 15s

If the app has two "Sign in" buttons (header and footer, for example), --unique will fail with exit 4 (AMBIGUOUS); pick the one you want with --nth 1 or tighten the selector. When IDs aren't stable, lean on the relational pseudo-classes:

mobax fill 'EditText:below(TextView[text=Email])'    "you@example.com"
mobax fill 'EditText:below(TextView[text=Password])' "hunter2"

fill waits for its field like tap does. Some fields refuse set-text while they are still opening (a search view, for one); fill then clicks the field, lets it settle and sets it again, and as a last resort types the text (ASCII) or pastes it (anything else).

If the field already has focus and you want the real keyboard path rather than atomic set-text, use type:

mobax type "you@example.com"
mobax submit

docs.title: Waiting for the next screen
docs.text:
mobax wait is overloaded by argument shape so it stays readable:

mobax wait idle 200ms        # block until the UI settles for 200 ms
mobax wait "Welcome"         # block until that text appears anywhere
mobax wait com.foo           # block until that package is in the foreground
mobax wait com.foo/.MainAct  # block on a specific activity
mobax wait 500ms             # client-side sleep (no daemon hop)
mobax wait '#results'        # block until a node matches a selector
mobax wait 'Button[text="OK"]'

Text waits match case-sensitively ("Battery Saver" isn't "Battery saver"); copy the label from mobax ui.

All forms honour --timeout. The default is 10 s — bump it for slow launches. Prefer these waits over shell sleep; a fixed sleep is both slower on fast devices and flaky on slow ones.

docs.title: Do then verify in one call
docs.text:
Tap a button and only succeed if the expected next state appears. This is the usual replacement for tap && sleep && wait chains:

mobax act --tap   "Send"          --until "Sent"             --timeout 8s
mobax act --fill  '[id=q]' "llm"  --until-selector RecyclerView --timeout 5s
mobax act --swipe up 300          --until-idle               --timeout 2s

Exit 0 only if both halves succeeded. TIMEOUT means the predicate never appeared; NOT_FOUND means the action itself could not execute.

docs.title: Retrying a flaky tap
docs.text:
Daemon-side waits get retried automatically when a TIMEOUT comes back, so the script stays linear:

mobax tap  "Refresh" --retries 4 --retry-delay 500ms --timeout 3s
mobax wait "Synced"  --retries 4 --timeout 5s

For unattended jobs, branch on the exit code instead of parsing stderr. There are only three codes worth a case arm:

mobax tap "Submit" --unique --timeout 5s
case $? in
  0)  echo "submitted" ;;
  2)  echo "no Submit button on screen" ;;        # NOT_FOUND
  3)  echo "tap acked but UI hung — escalating"   # TIMEOUT
      mobax see --size 768 /tmp/hung.jpg ;;
  4)  echo "ambiguous — narrow the selector" ;;   # AMBIGUOUS
  *)  echo "unexpected failure"; exit 1 ;;
esac

The full structured ErrCode (DAEMON_ERROR, PRECONDITION, SECURE_WINDOW, …) is preserved in --json output as error.code — use that when you need to dispatch on the long tail.

docs.title: Scrolling until something is visible
docs.text:
When the match is in the tree but below (or above) the screen, mobax tap swipes toward it and looks again, up to six times. Long lists only keep the rows near the screen in the tree, though (a RecyclerView recycles the rest), so for a row far down, scroll first. A 12-attempt scroll-then-tap loop in five lines:

for _ in $(seq 1 12); do
  mobax tap "Settings" --visible --unique --timeout 500ms && break
  mobax swipe up 250
done

If you already know one scroll is enough, batch the scroll and tap over a single warm socket:

mobax run - <<'EOF'
set timeout=500ms
swipe up 250
tap "Settings" --visible --unique
EOF

mobax run executes one command per line. Do not put multiple verbs on one line with semicolons. Use the shell for loop above when you need conditional looping.

docs.title: Debugging selectors
docs.text:
Start broad, inspect the JSON, then tighten. This is faster than guessing at coordinates.

mobax find 'Button:has-text("Continue")' --json | jq .
mobax find '*[text=Continue], *[text=Next]' --visible --json | jq .

If there are multiple matches, either make the selector structural or pick an index explicitly:

mobax tap 'Button:has-text("Continue"):in(LinearLayout[id~=footer])' --unique
mobax tap 'Button:has-text("Continue")' --visible --nth 2

docs.title: Two-factor SMS
docs.text:
mobax sms reads the inbox directly via IContentProvider — no installed helper app, no permission grants.

mobax wait "Enter the code"
CODE=$(mobax sms inbox --limit 1 --json | jq -r '.[0].body' | grep -oE '[0-9]{6}')
mobax type   "$CODE"
mobax submit

For apps that put the code on the clipboard, read or paste it directly:

CODE=$(mobax clip)
mobax type "$CODE"
mobax paste 'EditText:focused'

Clipboard watch is useful for magic-link and OTP handoff scripts:

mobax clip --watch --interval 250

docs.title: Notifications and push flows
docs.text:
Trigger a server-side push, then read recent notifications. Filter by package when you know it:

mobax notif com.example.app --limit 5 --json | jq .
mobax notif --history --limit 20 --json | jq .

For login links that open a browser or app, wait on the resulting package or activity instead of sleeping:

mobax wait com.example.app --timeout 15s
mobax wait com.example.app/.MainActivity --timeout 15s

docs.title: Running against many devices
docs.text:
mobax fan runs the same verb against each serial in parallel and exits non-zero if any device fails:

mobax fan PIXEL6,PIXEL7,EMU -- tap "Continue" --visible --timeout 5s

For machine-readable per-device output, add the global --json:

mobax --json fan PIXEL6,EMU -- wait "Welcome" --timeout 10s | jq -c

docs.title: Screenshotting on failure
docs.text:
A one-line bash -e trap that captures whatever was on screen the moment a verb failed. Use the fast 768px JPEG path for unattended runs:

set -e
trap 'mobax see --size 768 /tmp/mobileax-$$-failure.jpg' ERR

mobax tap  "Sign in" --unique
mobax wait "Dashboard" --timeout 10s

When you need a full artifact bundle for CI, collect the UI, device state, logs, and screenshot together:

DIR=/tmp/mobileax-failure-$$
mkdir -p "$DIR"
trap 'mobax ui --json > "$DIR/ui.json"; mobax ui --xml > "$DIR/ui.xml"; mobax info > "$DIR/info.txt"; mobax logs --tail 200 > "$DIR/logs.txt"; mobax see --size 768 "$DIR/screen.jpg"; echo "$DIR"' ERR

If you expect a black screenshot from a banking, password, or incognito screen, opt into the slower FLAG_SECURE check:

mobax see --secure-check --size 768 /tmp/secure-check.jpg

docs.title: Selectors when text alone isn't enough
docs.text:
Real Android UIs rarely give you stable resource IDs. Lean on the relational pseudo-classes:

# The OK button inside a specific dialog:
mobax tap '*[text="OK"]:in(LinearLayout[id~=dialog])' --unique

# The EditText below the "Email" label, visible only:
mobax tap 'EditText:below(TextView[text=Email]):visible' --unique

# Buttons near a specific icon:
mobax find 'Button:near(ImageView[desc~=cart], 200)'

# OR groups — "Continue" or "Next", whichever shipped this build:
mobax tap '*[text=Continue], *[text=Next]' --visible --unique --timeout 5s

# Playwright-style sugar:
mobax tap 'Button:has-text("Sign in")'
mobax tap 'Button:text-is("Sign in")'

docs.title: Driving from Python
docs.text:
There's a first-party SDK that wraps the CLI as a context manager and maps the exit codes to typed exceptions:

# pip install ./bindings/python  (from a checkout)
from mobileax import Session, NotFound, Timeout

with Session() as d:
    d.tap("Continue", visible=True, unique=True, timeout="5s")
    d.fill("[resource-id=com.example:id/email]", "you@example.com")
    d.submit()
    try:
        d.wait(text="Dashboard", timeout="15s")
    except Timeout:
        d.go("back")

For tight loops, the SDK opens a warm-socket batching context that shares one mobax run - subprocess across calls — per-call process startup collapses into one startup for the whole batch:

with Session() as d:
    with d.batch(timeout="5s", retries=2) as b:
        for label in labels:
            b.tap(label, visible=True)
        b.wait(text="Done")

For Node, Go, or anything else, drive mobax --json as a subprocess and parse one JSON line per call:

import json, subprocess
r = subprocess.run(
    ["mobax", "--json", "tap", "Sign in", "--visible", "--unique", "--timeout", "5s"],
    capture_output=True, text=True,
)
match r.returncode:
    case 0: print("tapped at", json.loads(r.stdout)["result"]["x"])
    case 2: raise RuntimeError("no Sign-in button on screen")
    case 3: raise TimeoutError("tap timed out")

docs.title: Batch scripts
docs.text:
For longer flows where the per-call socket churn matters, mobax run reads verb lines from a file (or stdin) and executes them over one warm socket. The set directives raise defaults without touching every line:

# flow.mobax
set timeout=8s
set retries=2
set continue-on-error
set dump-ttl=200ms

wait idle
tap   "Continue"   --visible --unique
fill  [id=email]   "you@example.com"
fill  [id=pw]      "hunter2"
submit
wait  "Dashboard"  --timeout 15s

mobax init my-flow.mobax       # scaffold a starter file
mobax run  my-flow.mobax       # run it

For ad-hoc batching, pipe directly:

printf '%s\n' 'tap "Refresh"' 'wait "Synced"' | mobax run -

docs.title: App lifecycle setup
docs.text:
Bring an app to the foreground, close it, or use raw shell commands for setup that is not yet a first-class verb. Pipe shell commands into mobax shell so streamed command output is drained correctly:

mobax open com.example.app/.MainActivity
mobax close com.example.app
printf '%s\n' 'pm clear com.example.app' | mobax shell

For deeplink-driven flows, inspect what the APK declares:

mobax links com.example.app
mobax open com.example.app/.MainActivity

docs.title: Emulators and the Android CLI
docs.text: mobileAX drives any device adb can see, API 28 or later. For emulators the recommended setup is Google's Android CLI (android) plus an AVD that renders on the host GPU.

docs.title: Android CLI
docs.text:
Install the android CLI (on Windows: winget install Google.AndroidCLI). mobax uses it to find adb, so nothing has to be on PATH:

android info                  # sdk: <path>  — adb is <path>/platform-tools/adb
android emulator list         # AVDs
android emulator start NAME   # returns once the emulator has booted
android emulator stop NAME

android emulator start takes --cold (skip the snapshot) and --headless (no window); android emulator create makes new AVDs (--help lists its options).

docs.title: Host GPU, always
docs.text:
Run emulators with host GPU rendering. android emulator start has no -gpu option, so set it in the AVD's config, ~/.android/avd/NAME.avd/config.ini:

hw.gpu.mode=host

Starting the emulator directly, pass it on the command line instead:

emulator -avd NAME -gpu host

To make it the default for every AVD, whoever starts it, turn the matching feature flags on in ~/.android/advancedFeatures.ini (create it if missing):

ForceGpuHost = on
Vulkan = on
GLDirectMem = on

ForceGpuHost puts the emulator on the host GPU even when the AVD says auto (the emulator's verbose log then shows gpu_mode_requested: host). Watch the spelling: the emulator silently ignores names it doesn't know, EnforceHostGPU included. Vulkan exposes host Vulkan to the guest; GLDirectMem maps guest GL buffers straight to host memory instead of copying them.

The default auto can choose a slower renderer. Every mirror frame is read back from the GPU (the daemon's main cost for stream), so the renderer shows up directly in frame rates, and numbers from different GPU modes aren't comparable.

docs.title: CPU and memory
docs.text:
The stock phone AVD has 4 cores and 2 GB. More helps: JPEG encoding, the app under test and SurfaceFlinger all share the guest's CPUs. In the same config.ini:

hw.cpu.ncore=6      # the emulator caps cores at 6
hw.ramSize=4096

On a Windows host (API 36 x86_64 AVD, 1080×2400, -gpu host) going from 4 cores / 2 GB to 6 cores / 4 GB took a native-size jpeg stream from 25–28 to 29–32 fps, --size 1200 from 42–50 to 56 fps, and h264 from 24 to 50 fps.

docs.title: Stream size
docs.text: At native resolution the mirror's GPU readback (25–36 ms per 1080×2400 frame on that host) caps a JPEG stream near 30 fps. Asking for a smaller frame cuts the readback, the encode and the decode together: mobax-viewer --size 1200 reaches about 56 fps, and the window rarely shows more pixels than that. h264 avoids the readback entirely.

docs.title: How mobax finds adb
docs.text:
In order, resolved once per process:

  1. $MOBILEAX_ADB, then $ADB
  2. ~/.mobileax/adb-path — the cached result of 3 (android info takes ~0.7 s)
  3. android info → <sdk>/platform-tools/adb
  4. $ANDROID_HOME, then $ANDROID_SDK_ROOT
  5. adb on PATH
  6. Android Studio's default SDK (~/Library/Android/sdk, ~/Android/Sdk, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Android\Sdk)

The last step is for MCP hosts and other GUI apps, which often start mobax without the shell's PATH. See also Sharp edges.

docs.title: Sharp edges
docs.text:
• Settings provider rejects our app_process identity; SettingsDirect uses IActivityManager.getContentProviderExternal (the cmd content path).
  • am start goes via IActivityTaskManager.startActivityAsUser with callingPackage="com.android.shell"; the system Context can't host startActivity from our anonymous process.
  • BroadcastReceiver registrations from our Context aren't routed — appCounts cache TTL'd at 4.5 s instead.
  • Most binder lookups go via reflection so the jar compiles against the public SDK. If a new SDK level renames a method, widen the matcher in the relevant helper.

docs.title: adb and the Android SDK
docs.text:
• Two SDKs on one machine (say Android Studio's and the one android info reports) ship different adb versions. Whichever client talks to the other's server kills and restarts it, which drops open connections and can hang a pipeline waiting on output. Point everything at one SDK, or pin MOBILEAX_ADB.
  • A set-but-empty ANDROID_HOME makes android info report an empty SDK path; mobax drops empty ANDROID_HOME / ANDROID_SDK_ROOT before asking it.
  • android emulator start has no -gpu flag; host GPU rendering has to come from hw.gpu.mode=host in the AVD's config.ini, or ForceGpuHost = on in ~/.android/advancedFeatures.ini (Emulators).
  • Running one AVD more than once needs -read-only on every instance, and a read-only emulator refuses snapshot save and load ("Snapshot save is disabled because "-read-only" was specified"). Keep the emulator you reset with snapshots as a single writable instance.
  • After a snapshot load or a reboot done by another tool, the daemon on the device may be gone. mobax and the MCP server start it again on the next call; @N refs from before are refused and the current screen comes back.
  • logcat -t N takes the last N lines before its priority, tag and regex filters, so logcat -t 50 *:E is often empty. mobax logs --level / --tag / --grep / --exclude reads the buffer and keeps the last N matching lines itself.
  • mobax logs --grep is logcat's own regex (ECMAScript, on the device). It has no case-insensitive flag, so -i spells each letter both ways ([aA]); letters at the ends of a class range like [a-z] stay as written. --exclude is plain text, matched on the host.
  • mobax logs --since 5m reads the device's clock, not the host's.

docs.title: Wire reference
docs.text:
The on-device daemon speaks a length-prefixed binary protocol: each frame is uint32 big-endian length + payload (in both directions). Commands are ASCII text, verb [k=v …] style. This document lists every wire verb the daemon dispatches in src/dev/mobileax/daemon/Server.java.

Use these directly via mobax do <wire> or mobax shell (one socket, many commands). ERR:<msg> is returned on failure.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
ping                                                  → pong
info                                                  → "<srcW> <srcH>"
quit                                                  → bye   (daemon exits)

docs.title: Inspect — accessibility tree
docs.text:
dump                                                  full JSON dump, every window
dump_active                                           active window only

docs.title: Capture — screenshots and streams
docs.text:
screenshot returns one frame; the stream_* verbs hold the socket open and push continuously.

screenshot       [size=N] [q=N] [fmt=jpeg|webp|png] [max=1] [secure_check=1]
stream           [size=N] [q=N] [fps=N]                  JPEG, native by default
stream_h264      [size=N] [max=1] [fps=N] [bitrate=KBPS] [gop=SEC]
stream_tilejpeg  [size=N] [q=N] [tile=N]
keyframe                                                 force IDR on all H.264 streams

size=N = long edge in pixels, default 768. q clamps to [1, 100], default 80. fmt=jpeg is the default and preferred hot path for agents. fmt=webp is available for compact lossy exports, though it may encode slower than JPEG on emulators. fmt=png is intended for debug/export only; Android's PNG encoder is much slower than JPEG. max=1 = native resolution (overrides size). secure_check=1 enables an extra FLAG_SECURE probe for suspiciously small black frames; it is off by default because it shells out to dumpsys window.

docs.text:
tap         x=NUM y=NUM
swipe       x1=NUM y1=NUM x2=NUM y2=NUM [dur=MS]
swipe_dir   left|right|up|down [dur=MS]                  60% travel from screen centre
down        x=NUM y=NUM                                  pointer down (sticks)
move        x=NUM y=NUM
up          x=NUM y=NUM                                  releases the down pointer
scroll      x=NUM y=NUM dy=NUM                           wheel scroll at point
key         NAME                                         e.g. BACK, HOME, ENTER
key         code=N                                       raw KeyEvent code
                                                         key/scroll take wait=0: don't wait for the
                                                         window to handle it or for animations to
                                                         end (a live viewer; Back in Recents took 5 s)

                                                         (KeyEvents for a password field or a
                                                         view with no editable focus)

docs.title: Waits — event-driven, no polling
docs.text:
wait_for_idle      [idle_ms=200] [timeout_ms=5000]     → ok elapsed=N idle=M | ERR:timeout
                                                         elapsed: ms waited; idle: ms the
                                                         screen had been quiet by then
event_seq                                              → seq=N  (events seen so far)
settle             since=N [first_ms=200] [idle_ms=120] [timeout_ms=1500]
                                                       → ok elapsed=N changed=0|1 | ERR:TIMEOUT
                                                         read event_seq before an action, then
                                                         settle: waits up to first_ms for the
                                                         action's first event, then idle_ms of
                                                         quiet; changed=0 when nothing happened
settle_dump        since=N [first_ms=200] [idle_ms=120] [timeout_ms=1500]
                                                       → ok elapsed=N changed=0|1 moving=0|1
                                                         then a newline and the `dump` JSON
                                                         settle, then the screen once it holds
                                                         still: while an app window reaches past
                                                         the screen's edge (sliding in) it waits
                                                         for the next event, and two dumps 40 ms
                                                         apart must agree; moving=1: never quiet
wait_for_text      text="…" [match=sub|exact] [scope=all|app|active] [timeout_ms=5000]
                                                       → ok x=… y=… w=… h=… elapsed=…
wait_for_activity  n=COMPONENT [timeout_ms=5000]       prefix-matches the package

docs.title: Composites
docs.text:
Tap then await the UI to settle — saves a wire round-trip versus tap + wait_for_idle.

tap_and_dump   x=NUM y=NUM [idle_ms=200] [timeout_ms=2000]   → dump_active JSON
tap_and_settle x=NUM y=NUM [idle_ms=200] [timeout_ms=2000]   → ok elapsed=N idle=M

docs.title: State — push-mirrored snapshot
docs.text:
ui_watch [min_ms=250] [moves=0|1] keeps the socket and pushes the window tree (the dump payload) each time it changes: {"seq":N,"ev":EVENTS,"dump":{…}}. Driven by accessibility events, not polling; a dump equal to the last one is not sent, frames are at least min_ms apart (floor 50), the last change is always sent, and a slow reader gets only the newest frame. Changes in position only (an animation, a scroll in flight) are held until events have been quiet for 300 ms, then sent once with the resting positions; moves=1 sends them as they happen. Hang up to stop.

state reads a single field from the cached snapshot the daemon maintains via accessibility / lifecycle hooks. state_watch keeps the socket open and pushes a fresh JSON frame on every state change.

state interactive | battery_level | battery_charging | top | procs | device | device_fresh
state_watch                                            chunked JSON frames

docs.title: Quoting and escaping
docs.text:
• Arguments are split on ASCII whitespace.
  • "..." quoted strings are honoured for text="…" / value="…" and similar — useful when the value contains spaces or =.
  • Selectors are passed as-is; quote any embedded whitespace.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Every failure path returns a single frame whose payload starts with ERR: followed by a short tag (e.g. ERR:tap_and_dump-needs-x-y). Streamed responses send the ERR: frame then the len=0 terminator.

docs.title: 데몬 단일 루퍼 + Gradle 빌드 Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: on-device 데몬을 MainLooper 하나 + 작은 Work 풀 구조의 Kotlin 코루틴 모델로 바꾸고, Gradle이 build/hs.jar를 만드는 정식 빌드가 되게 한다. 와이어 프로토콜은 바이트 단위로 유지.

Architecture: Looper.loop()를 도는 main 스레드가 MessageQueue.addOnFileDescriptorEventListener(epoll)로 소켓·파이프를 감시하고, 연결마다 Dispatchers.Main 위의 코루틴 하나가 readFrame → dispatch → respond를 suspend로 처리한다. CPU/장시간 binder 작업만 Work 디스패처로 보낸다. 중간 단계에서는 아직 포팅 안 된 블로킹 Java 핸들러를 Legacy 디스패처 + 블로킹 스트림 어댑터로 돌려 매 태스크마다 jar가 동작하게 하고, 마지막에 Legacy를 제거한다.

Tech Stack: Kotlin 2.2.21 (JVM target 17), kotlinx-coroutines-core/android (최신 안정 1.10.x), Gradle(Kotlin DSL, 기존 wrapper), SDK R8(build-tools/36.0.0/lib/d8.jar), JUnit5 + kotlinx-coroutines-test (JVM 단위 테스트), Python 3 (scripts/wire-smoke.py, 기기 통합 테스트), AVD Medium_Phone(API 36).

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-25-daemon-looper-gradle-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• 와이어 프로토콜(docs/wire.md): verb, 인자, 응답 바이트, uint32 BE length + payload 프레이밍, ERR: 문자열, 스트림 len=0 종결자, __exit__ N 트레일러 — 전부 기존과 동일. MAX_CMD = 256, 위반 시 BAD_ARG:bad-length:<len> 후 연결 종료.
  • 엔트리: dev.handsets.daemon.Main.main(String[]), --port=N(기본 9008), 127.0.0.1 바인드, backlog 8, SO_REUSEADDR, TCP_NODELAY. stdout에 hsd listening on 127.0.0.1:<port> 와 hsd ready (sdk=<N>) 출력 유지.
  • 산출물: build/hs.jar (dex만), --min-api 28, R8 --release. 크기 목표: 기준 jar 대비 +300KB 이내, 초과 시 보고.
  • R8: SDK build-tools/<ver>/lib/d8.jar의 com.android.tools.r8.R8를 JavaExec로 실행. 기본 build-tools 36.0.0, -PbuildTools=로 변경.
  • 루퍼(main)에서 금지: 덤프, 인코딩, Thread.sleep, 블로킹 소켓/파이프 I/O, 상한 없는 binder 호출. 애매하면 Work.
  • 스레드 최종 상태: main + Work 풀(min(4, availableProcessors)) (+ 프레임워크 binder/MediaCodec 스레드). hs-ua는 main looper 시도가 실패할 때만 예외로 허용하고 보고.
  • 이미지/상태 스트림(stream, stream_tilejpeg, state_watch, clip_watch)은 최신 프레임만 유지. stream_h264는 공유 전까지 프레임 무손실 + 연결별 backpressure.
  • 호스트 코드(handsets-cli, handsets-tui, handsets-viewer, bindings/) 수정 금지.
  • 검증 기기: AVD Medium_Phone (API 36, x86_64) 하나. adb: E:\packages\Android\Sdk\platform-tools\adb.exe.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. TCP 단편화: 명령 프레임의 4바이트 길이/페이로드가 여러 read로 쪼개져 도착 → 하나의 명령으로 정상 처리. (Task 3 ConnTest.fragmentedFrame)
  2. 스트림 중 클라이언트 강제 종료: stream*/state_watch/logcat/shell 중 소켓이 끊김 → 구독 해제, 서브프로세스 kill, 인코더/VirtualDisplay 해제, 다른 연결 영향 없음. (Task 3 ConnTest.cancelOnEof, Task 9 smoke disconnect_cleanup)
  3. 느린/읽지 않는 클라이언트: 스트림을 열고 읽지 않는 클라이언트가 있어도 다른 연결의 ping p95 < 50ms. (Task 3 ConnTest.latestOnlyReplaces, Task 8 smoke slow_client)
  4. 설치 중 업로드 중단: install size=N 후 N바이트를 다 보내기 전에 끊김 → 세션 abandon, 데몬 정상. (Task 6 smoke install_truncated)
  5. UTF-8 / 경계 길이 명령: CJK clip_set, text, 길이 정확히 256/257 프레임 → 기존과 같은 응답. (Task 4 DispatchTest.cjkAndLengthBounds, smoke 케이스)

docs.title: File Structure
docs.text:
새 Kotlin 파일 (src/dev/handsets/daemon/, 패키지 dev.handsets.daemon):

파일 책임 Loop.kt Main/Work/Legacy 디스패처, 루트 scope, onMain {} 헬퍼 IoLoop.kt IoLoop 인터페이스 + MessageQueueIoLoop(Android), fd 획득 Fds Conn.kt 비블로킹 연결: suspend 읽기, 출력 큐(backpressure / latest-only), 종료 HsServer.kt accept 루프, 연결별 코루틴 Dispatch.kt verb 디스패치 (기존 Server.handle switch + run* 포팅) Args.kt 기존 Server의 순수 파싱 헬퍼(strArg, longArg, positional, parseInputArgs, …) 포팅 Main.kt 엔트리, 초기화 순서, Looper.loop() (기존 Main.java 대체) Waits.kt UiEvents + WaitRegistry 대체 (suspend) StateRefresher.kt Debouncer + State 리프레시/구독 fan-out ProcStream.kt 서브프로세스 stdout을 IoLoop로 읽어 청크 프레임 전송 Streams.kt stream/stream_tilejpeg/stream_h264/state_watch/clip_watch 세션 LegacyStreams.kt 임시: Conn ↔ 블로킹 DataInputStream/DataOutputStream 어댑터 (Task 9에서 삭제)

삭제: Server.java, Main.java, UiEvents.java, WaitRegistry.java, Streamer.java, LocalIntentSender.java (각 해당 태스크에서). 테스트: test/dev/handsets/daemon/*Test.kt (JVM, android 미사용 코드만). 스크립트: scripts/wire-smoke.py.

docs.text:
Files: - Create: src/dev/handsets/daemon/Loop.kt, IoLoop.kt, Conn.kt - Test: test/dev/handsets/daemon/ConnTest.kt, test/dev/handsets/daemon/SelectorIoLoop.kt(테스트용 IoLoop 구현)

Interfaces: - Produces: - Loop.kt: object Loop { val Main: CoroutineDispatcher; val Work: CoroutineDispatcher; val Legacy: CoroutineDispatcher; val scope: CoroutineScope; fun init(main: CoroutineDispatcher = Dispatchers.Main.immediate) } — Work = 고정 min(4, cpu) 데몬 스레드 풀(hs-work-N) .asCoroutineDispatcher(), Legacy = 캐시드 풀(hs-legacy-N, Task 9에서 제거). scope = CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Main + CoroutineExceptionHandler{ 로그 }). init이 Dispatchers.Main 해석 실패 시 Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()).asCoroutineDispatcher("hs-main")로 대체하고 어느 쪽인지 stderr에 hsd dispatcher: main=<kind> 출력. - IoLoop.kt: interface IoLoop { fun watch(fd: FileDescriptor, events: Int, cb: (fd: FileDescriptor, events: Int) -> Int); fun unwatch(fd: FileDescriptor) } (events/반환값 의미는 MessageQueue.OnFileDescriptorEventListener와 동일: EVENT_INPUT=1, EVENT_OUTPUT=2, EVENT_ERROR=4, 0 반환 = 해제). class MessageQueueIoLoop(queue: MessageQueue) : IoLoop. object Fds { fun of(ch: SelectableChannel): FileDescriptor } — Android SocketChannelImpl/ServerSocketChannelImpl의 getFD()를 리플렉션으로 호출. - Conn.kt: class Conn(ch: SocketChannel, io: IoLoop) { suspend fun readInt(): Int; suspend fun readFully(n: Int): ByteArray; suspend fun readChunk(max: Int): ByteArray? /* null=EOF */; suspend fun send(payload: ByteArray) /* 프레임(len+payload) 큐잉, 큐 바이트 > OUT_LIMIT(4 MiB)이면 drain까지 suspend */; suspend fun sendRaw(bytes: ByteArray) /* 길이 접두 없이 */; fun sendLatest(slot: Int, payload: ByteArray) /* 같은 slot의 아직 안 나간 프레임을 교체 */; suspend fun flush(); val job: Job /* EOF/에러/close 시 cancel */; fun close() }. 읽기 EOF는 EOFException을 던진다.

  • [ ] Step 1: 실패하는 테스트 작성 — ConnTest (JVM, SelectorIoLoop가 별도 스레드에서 java.nio.channels.Selector로 IoLoop 계약을 흉내, 디스패처는 단일 스레드 executor):
  • fragmentedFrame: 클라이언트가 [0,0,0,4]를 2바이트씩, "ping"을 1바이트씩 보냄 → readInt()==4, String(readFully(4))=="ping".
  • sendFramesInOrder: send("a"), send("bb") → 클라이언트가 00000001 61 00000002 6262 수신.
  • backpressureSuspends: 클라이언트가 읽지 않을 때 send를 반복하면 누적 큐 바이트가 OUT_LIMIT+최대 프레임 1개를 넘지 않음(초과 시점에 suspend 확인 — withTimeoutOrNull(200){ send(big) } == null).
  • latestOnlyReplaces: 읽지 않는 클라이언트에 sendLatest(0, f1..f50) → 클라이언트가 읽기 시작하면 받은 프레임 수 ≤ 3 이고 마지막이 f50.
  • cancelOnEof: 클라이언트 close → conn.job.isCancelled 가 1초 내 true, 진행 중 readInt()는 EOFException/취소로 끝남.
  • [ ] Step 2: Run: ./gradlew test --tests '*ConnTest*' — Expected: FAIL (클래스 없음).
  • [ ] Step 3: Loop.kt, IoLoop.kt, Conn.kt 구현. Conn은 읽기 대기 시 EVENT_INPUT, 출력 큐가 비어 있지 않을 때만 EVENT_OUTPUT을 watch(쓰기 가능할 때마다 non-blocking write). 소켓은 configureBlocking(false), TCP_NODELAY.
  • [ ] Step 4: Run: ./gradlew test --tests '*ConnTest*' — Expected: PASS.

docs.title: 데몬 단일 루퍼 리팩토링 + Gradle 빌드 전환 — 설계
docs.text: 날짜: 2026-10-25 · 대상: src/dev/handsets/daemon/ (on-device daemon, hs.jar)

docs.title: 1. 의도와 이유
docs.text:
on-device 데몬은 지금 잘 동작하지만, 구조가 "필요할 때마다 스레드 하나"로 자라 왔다.

  • Server: 블로킹 accept() + 연결당 hs-conn 스레드, 블로킹 DataInputStream/DataOutputStream, 곳곳의 synchronized (out).
  • HandlerThread 다수: hs-ua(UiAutomation), State의 hs-state-pkg / hs-state-display / hs-state-cfg, Screenshot 미러마다 hs-mirror-listener-*.
  • State refresher 스레드(wait/notify + Thread.sleep 디바운스), Main의 warmup 스레드.
  • Dumpsys / Logcat / ShellExec / Lifecycle의 서브프로세스 리더 스레드.
  • Streamer / TileStreamer / state_watch 의 연결별 BlockingQueue 루프, WaitRegistry의 lock.wait, LocalIntentSender.await 블로킹.

사용자가 체감하는 문제는 없다. 동기는 아키텍처적 불필요함의 제거다: Android가 원래 제공하는 MainLooper + MessageQueue(epoll) 모델 하나로 이벤트를 모으고, 진짜 CPU 작업(버퍼/이미지 복사, 인코딩, 덤프 직렬화)만 작은 풀로 보낸다.

동시에, 지금은 IDE 전용인 Gradle 프로젝트를 실제 hs.jar를 만드는 정식 빌드로 만든다.

docs.title: 2. 목표 / 비목표 / 안티목표
docs.text:
목표 - 메인 스레드 하나가 Looper.loop()를 돌고, 모든 I/O·이벤트·타이머가 이 루퍼 위에서 처리된다. - 루퍼는 절대 블로킹되지 않는다 (사용자 결정). 오래 기다리는 요청은 모두 suspend/콜백으로 바뀐다. - CPU 작업만 작은 고정 크기 풀에서 수행한다. - Kotlin + kotlinx-coroutines, Dispatchers.Main 기반 (사용자 결정). - Gradle(./gradlew)이 javac/kotlinc → R8 → dex → build/hs.jar까지 만든다.

비목표 - 와이어 프로토콜 변경. docs/wire.md의 모든 verb, 인자, 응답, 프레이밍, 에러 문자열은 바이트 단위로 유지 (사용자 결정). 호스트 쪽(handsets-cli, handsets-tui, handsets-viewer, bindings/python)은 수정하지 않는다. - 새 기능 추가, 성능 튜닝(회귀가 없는 선에서). - 모든 Java 파일의 Kotlin 변환. - 외부 privileged-process 프레임워크 도입 (예: priv-kit). priv-kit은 설치된 앱(AAR, Compose UI)이 자기 권한 프로세스를 띄우는 Shizuku 계열 구조라, 앱 없이 호스트가 app_process jar를 직접 띄우는 이 데몬과 모델이 다르다. 의존성으로 쓰지 않고 필요하면 아이디어만 참고한다.

안티목표 (동작해도 실패로 보는 것) - 메인 루퍼에서 binder 장시간 호출, 덤프, 인코딩, Thread.sleep, 블로킹 소켓 I/O가 일어나는 것. - 한 클라이언트가 느리거나 멈췄을 때 다른 연결이 지연되는 것. - 클라이언트 쪽에서 응답 차이가 관찰되는 것 (hs 명령 결과가 달라짐). - tap 등 hot path 지연이 기존보다 눈에 띄게 나빠지는 것. - hs.jar가 과도하게 커지는 것 (기준: 기존 대비 +300KB 이내를 목표, 초과 시 보고).

docs.title: 3. 제약
docs.text:
• 실행 환경: CLASSPATH=/data/local/tmp/hs.jar app_process /system/bin dev.handsets.daemon.Main --port=N (shell UID). 엔트리 dev.handsets.daemon.Main.main(String[]) 시그니처·클래스명 유지.
  • 산출물 위치 build/hs.jar 유지 (handsets-cli/src/daemon.rs가 이 경로를 찾고, .github/workflows/release.yml이 업로드).
  • --min-api 28 유지. Kotlin JVM target은 R8/D8이 desugar 가능한 범위(11 또는 17)로.
  • binder 스레드풀은 app_process가 만들므로 제거 대상이 아니다.
  • SDK: local.properties의 sdk.dir (현재 E:\packages\Android\Sdk, platforms 36 / 37.0 / 37.2, build-tools 35 / 36).
  • 작업 시작 시 워킹트리에 커밋되지 않은 Gradle 초안(build.gradle.kts, settings.gradle.kts, gradle/, gradlew*, proguard-rules.pro, local.properties)과 build.sh / README.md / Screenshot.java 수정이 있다. 이것을 출발점으로 삼는다.

docs.title: 4.1 스레드 모델
docs.text:
스레드 역할 main (Looper) 소켓 accept/read/write, 서브프로세스 stdout, a11y 이벤트, display/broadcast 리스너, ImageReader 콜백, 타이머, 모든 코루틴의 기본 실행지 work pool (작은 고정 크기, 예: min(4, cpu)) JPEG/WebP/PNG 인코딩, 비트맵/버퍼 복사, dump/dump_active 트리 순회+JSON, 길어질 수 있는 동기 binder 호출 MediaCodec 내부 / binder 스레드 프레임워크 소유, 관여하지 않음
  • Main: prepareMainLooper() → 초기화 → Looper.loop(). hs-ua HandlerThread 제거, UiAutomation은 main looper로 생성 — 먼저 시도 (사용자 결정).
  • 주의: UiAutomation.connect()는 서비스 연결 콜백(UA의 looper로 post됨)을 블로킹 대기한다. 따라서 main looper를 쓰려면 Looper.loop()가 돈 뒤에 connect를 Work 스레드에서 호출하고, connect 완료 후 UA 의존 핸들러들을 main에서 초기화한다. 서버 accept는 그 전에 열어도 되지만 UA가 필요한 verb는 준비될 때까지 suspend.
  • 기기(API 36)에서 이 방식이 안정적으로 동작하지 않으면 hs-ua HandlerThread 하나를 예외로 남기고, UA 이벤트 콜백은 즉시 main으로 post한다. 어느 쪽인지 결과를 보고한다.
  • 코루틴: 루트 CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.Main.immediate). CPU 작업은 withContext(Work) (Work = 위 고정 풀을 asCoroutineDispatcher()로 감싼 것, 또는 Dispatchers.Default.limitedParallelism(n)).
  • Dispatchers.Main 해석: kotlinx-coroutines-android의 ServiceLoader 경로가 app_process/dex-only jar에서 동작해야 한다. R8이 META-INF/services/kotlinx.coroutines.internal.MainDispatcherFactory를 입력으로 받아 치환하게 한다. 기기에서 확인 실패 시 Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()).asCoroutineDispatcher()로 대체하고 Main이라는 이름의 val로 노출한다 (내 판단).

docs.title: 4.2 이벤트 루프 I/O 계층 (신규, Kotlin)
docs.text:
• 서버 소켓: ServerSocketChannel non-blocking, 127.0.0.1, backlog 8, SO_REUSEADDR. fd를 Looper.getMainLooper().queue.addOnFileDescriptorEventListener(fd, EVENT_INPUT, …)로 등록해 accept.
  • fd 얻기: ParcelFileDescriptor.fromSocket / 리플렉션 등 구현자가 동작하는 방법을 고른다. 대안으로 android.system.Os.socket/bind/listen/accept + FileDescriptor 직접 사용도 허용 (구현자 재량).
  • 연결(Conn): non-blocking 소켓 + 입력 버퍼 + 출력 큐.
  • suspend fun readInt(), readFully(n), readFrame() — 버퍼가 부족하면 EVENT_INPUT을 기다리며 suspend.
  • fun send(frame) / suspend fun sendAndDrain() — 출력 큐에 넣고 EVENT_OUTPUT으로 흘림. 큐 상한을 넘으면 suspend (backpressure).
  • 이미지·상태 스트림(stream, stream_tilejpeg, state_watch, clip_watch)은 "최신 것만 유지" 정책: 이전 프레임이 아직 안 나갔으면 새 프레임으로 교체 (현재 BlockingQueue(1)/drop-oldest 동작과 동일한 의미).
  • stream_h264 (1단계, 현재와 동일): 연결마다 인코더 하나, 프레임을 버리지 않는다 (P-frame 손실은 디코딩을 깨뜨림). 연결별 bounded 출력 큐 + backpressure로 그 연결의 인코더 드레인만 멈춘다.
  • 스트림 공유 (사용자 요청, 여유가 되면 마지막 단계로): 같은 파라미터의 스트림 클라이언트들이 하나의 소스/인코더 출력을 공유한다.
    • stream_h264: 정규화한 파라미터(출력 크기, fps, bitrate, gop)가 같은 연결들은 인코더 + VirtualDisplay 하나를 공유. 인코더가 낸 access unit 버퍼를 한 번 복사해 불변 ByteArray로 만들고 모든 구독 연결에 같은 참조를 넣는다. 파라미터가 다르면 별도 인코더. 마지막 구독자가 나가면 해제.
    • 새 구독자 합류: 캐시해 둔 codec config(SPS/PPS)와 현재 연결이 기대하는 시작 프레임(현재 와이어가 첫 프레임 전에 보내는 것이 있다면 그것)을 먼저 보내고, 인코더에 IDR을 요청한 뒤 다음 IDR부터 전달.
    • 느린 구독자: 공유 인코더는 한 클라이언트 때문에 멈출 수 없으므로, 연결별 큐가 상한을 넘으면 그 연결의 대기 프레임을 버리고 다음 IDR까지 skip + IDR 요청 (해당 클라이언트만 잠깐 멈춘 듯 보이고 깨진 화면은 없음 — 내 판단).
    • stream/stream_tilejpeg도 같은 원칙: (size, q, tile)이 같으면 프레임당 인코딩 한 번, 결과 바이트를 공유.
    • keyframe verb는 활성 인코더 전부에 IDR 요청, 응답 ok n=의 n은 연결 수를 유지 (와이어 호환 — 내 판단).
  • TCP_NODELAY 유지.
  • EOF/에러/EVENT_ERROR → 연결 Job 취소 → 그 연결의 대기, 스트림, 서브프로세스, 구독이 전부 정리된다 (try/finally/invokeOnCompletion).
  • 연결 하나 = 코루틴 하나. 그 안에서 기존 Server.handle과 같은 순서로 readFrame → dispatch → respond를 반복. 같은 연결에서 명령은 순차, 연결 간에는 독립.
  • 서브프로세스(dumpsys, logcat, shell, monitor, location/settings 내부 호출 등): Process stdout fd를 같은 방식으로 등록해 읽고 청크 프레임으로 전달. 프로세스 종료 대기도 블로킹 waitFor() 대신 EOF 후 exitValue() 또는 풀에서 waitFor.
  • stdout fd 얻는 방법은 구현자 재량 (ProcessBuilder 대신 Os.pipe + android.system.Os/리플렉션 ProcessImpl 등). 깔끔한 방법이 없으면 서브프로세스 읽기에 한해 풀 스레드에서 블로킹 read 후 main으로 post 하는 것을 허용 (루퍼는 여전히 안 막힘).

docs.title: 4.3 블로킹 지점의 재작성
docs.text:
현재 변경 WaitRegistry.awaitIdle/awaitPredicate (lock.wait) main에서 a11y 이벤트 수신 → 대기자 목록 재평가. idle은 postDelayed/delay 타이머로, predicate 재평가는 이벤트마다. predicate가 노드 조회(binder)라면 withContext(Work)로. suspend API로 노출. LocalIntentSender.await(ms) (BlockingQueue) — Installer, Pm CompletableDeferred<Intent> + withTimeoutOrNull. install/install_multi/push의 APK·파일 청크 수신 Conn.readFully suspend로 읽고, 세션/파일 쓰기는 Work에서. State refresher 스레드 markDirty()가 main에서 debounce Job 재시작(DEBOUNCE_MS) + heartbeat는 HEARTBEAT_MS 반복 코루틴. computeDevice()는 Work에서, 결과 저장·구독자 fan-out은 main에서. State pkg/display/cfg HandlerThread 3개 모두 main Handler에 등록. Screenshot 미러별 HandlerThread ImageReader.setOnImageAvailableListener(…, mainHandler). 이미지 획득 직후 버퍼 복사·인코딩은 Work. Streamer / TileStreamer / H264Streamer 연결 루프 프레임 이벤트 → Channel(CONFLATED) → 연결 코루틴이 fps/IDLE_INTERVAL_MS 타이밍으로 Work에서 인코딩 후 Conn으로 전송. H.264는 MediaCodec 출력 드레인을 콜백(setCallback(…, mainHandler)) 또는 Work로. state_watch, clip_watch 큐 루프 구독 콜백 → conflated 채널 → 전송. warmup 스레드 scope.launch(Work) { dumper.dumpActive() }. Main.connectWithRetry의 Thread.sleep(250) 루퍼 시작 전 초기화 단계이므로 그대로 둬도 됨 (내 판단). Input의 swipe dur=, tap 등 UiAutomation injectInputEvent 이벤트 간 지연은 delay(). injectInputEvent(sync=true)가 길어질 수 있으면 Work에서 (구현자가 측정해 결정).
  • 루퍼에서 직접 실행해도 되는 동기 binder 호출의 기준: 짧고 상한이 있는 시스템 서비스 조회 (getprop, settings get, pm path 등). 그 외(덤프, provider query, 패키지 목록 등 수십 ms 이상 걸릴 수 있는 것)는 Work. 애매하면 Work (내 판단).
  • 공유 상태는 main에서만 변경하는 것을 원칙으로 하고, 그 결과 불필요해진 synchronized/volatile/CopyOnWriteArrayList는 제거한다. 풀에서 만지는 객체(인코더 버퍼 등)는 해당 작업 안에서만 소유.

docs.title: 4.4 언어와 코드 배치
docs.text:
• Kotlin으로 새로 쓰는 것: Main(엔트리는 @JvmStatic 또는 object Main으로 dev.handsets.daemon.Main.main 유지), 이벤트 루프/Conn/서버, 디스패치(기존 Server의 verb 파싱·응답 문자열은 그대로 이식), State, UiEvents/WaitRegistry, 스트리머들, Installer/Pm/LocalIntentSender, 서브프로세스 스트리밍(Dumpsys/Logcat/ShellExec/Lifecycle).
  • Java로 유지: 동기 헬퍼(Props, Wm, Binders, Am, SettingsDirect, SettingsApi, Providers, Manifest, JsonOut, Traverse, Dumper, NodeActions, Clipboard, Notifications, Location, Files 등). 내부의 synchronized는 호출 경로가 단일화된 뒤 필요 없으면 제거해도 되고 남겨도 무방.
  • 소스 위치: src/ 루트에 Java·Kotlin 공존 유지 (현재 Gradle 초안과 같음). 패키지 dev.handsets.daemon.

docs.title: 4.5 Gradle 빌드
docs.text:
• build.gradle.kts를 IDE 전용에서 정식 빌드로:
  • kotlin("jvm") + java-library, android.jar compileOnly/bootclasspath. compileSdk는 -PandroidCompileSdk 또는 설치된 최신 numeric 플랫폼 (현재 초안의 하드코딩 37.2 정리).
  • 의존성: kotlin-stdlib, kotlinx-coroutines-core + kotlinx-coroutines-android 최신 안정판 (현재 1.3.9 → 업그레이드).
  • 태스크 hsJar: 컴파일 클래스 + 런타임 의존성 jar → R8(--release --min-api 28 --lib android.jar --pg-conf proguard-rules.pro) → classes.dex → build/hs.jar (dex 하나만, 필요 시 META-INF/services는 R8 처리 후 불필요).
    • R8 실행 수단: SDK의 R8 (사용자 결정). .bat 래퍼 대신 SDK build-tools/<ver>/lib/d8.jar(R8 메인 클래스 com.android.tools.r8.R8 포함)를 JavaExec로 실행 — Windows/macOS/Linux CI 공통 (내 판단). build-tools 버전은 -PbuildTools= 또는 설치된 최신; 기본 36.0.0.
  • proguard-rules.pro: 기존 build.sh의 r8.pro 내용(Main keep, -repackageclasses '', -allowaccessmodification, -dontwarn **) + 코루틴 규칙.
  • assemble/build가 hsJar에 의존. Gradle 자체 출력은 지금 초안처럼 build-gradle/에 두되 최종 jar는 build/hs.jar로 복사.
  • build.sh: ./gradlew hsJar 호출하는 얇은 래퍼로 축소 (기존 사용자·문서 호환).
  • CI .github/workflows/release.yml: JDK 셋업 + ./gradlew hsJar (또는 래퍼 build.sh 그대로 호출). 산출물 경로 동일.
  • README.md의 "Daemon IDE setup" 섹션과 docs/architecture.md의 build.sh 설명을 갱신.
  • local.properties는 머신 로컬 파일이므로 git 추적에서 제외하는 것이 맞다 (현재 staged 상태 — 내 판단, 구현 시 unstage + .gitignore).

docs.title: 5. 검증
docs.text:
검증 방법은 사용자가 구현자에게 맡겼다. 결정:

  1. 빌드: ./gradlew hsJar 성공, build/hs.jar에 classes.dex만, 크기 기록 (기존 build.sh 산출물과 비교).
  2. 환경: 기존 AVD Medium_Phone(API 36, x86_64, E:\packages\Android\Sdk\emulator) 하나만 기동. min-api 28은 유지하되 버전 매트릭스 검증은 하지 않는다 (사용자 결정: 상위 버전에서 현재 잘 동작하므로 충분). 호스트 CLI는 handsets-cli를 cargo build --release로 빌드해 사용 (HANDSETS_JAR로 jar 지정).
  3. 와이어 스모크 테스트 스크립트 scripts/wire-smoke.py (신규): adb forward 후 소켓으로 docs/wire.md의 verb들을 직접 호출, 응답을 정규화(타임스탬프·elapsed·배터리 등 변동값 마스킹)해 저장. 기존 jar(현재 HEAD를 build.sh로 빌드)와 새 jar 결과를 diff. 최소 커버리지:
  4. 단발: ping info dump dump_active screenshot(jpeg/png) tap swipe key text getprop settings_get wm_info pm_list pm_path state * clip_get/clip_set deeplinks sms/calls/contacts
  5. 대기: wait_for_idle wait_for_text(성공/timeout) wait_for_activity tap_and_dump tap_and_settle
  6. 스트림: stream/stream_h264/stream_tilejpeg N프레임 수신 후 끊기, state_watch, clip_watch, logcat/dumpsys/shell 청크+종결자, pull/push 라운드트립, install(작은 테스트 APK)
  7. 동시성: 스트림 하나를 일부러 읽지 않는 느린 클라이언트로 열어 둔 상태에서 다른 연결의 ping/tap 지연이 정상인지, 장시간 wait_for_text timeout_ms=5000 중 다른 연결 ping이 즉시 응답하는지.
  8. 연결 정리: 스트림 중 클라이언트 강제 종료 후 데몬 스레드 수/구독자 수가 원복되는지.
  9. 스레드 수 확인: adb shell ls /proc/<pid>/task + cat comm로 기존/신규 비교, hs-* 스레드가 main + work pool만 남았는지.
  10. 지연: scripts/bench-adb.sh(또는 smoke 스크립트 내 tap/dump_active/screenshot 100회 p50/p95) 기존 대비 회귀 없음.
  11. 수동 확인: hs TUI/뷰어 미러링이 정상 동작.

docs.title: 6. 구현자 재량으로 남긴 것
docs.text:
• fd 이벤트 등록에 쓸 소켓/파이프 fd 획득 방식 (4.2).
  • Work 풀 크기와 구현 (Executors 기반 vs limitedParallelism).
  • 어떤 동기 호출을 main에 둘지의 세부 판단 (4.3 기준 안에서).
  • 파일/클래스 분할과 이름, Java 헬퍼 중 추가로 Kotlin화할 것.
  • 작업 순서. 단, 매 단계에서 hs.jar가 빌드·동작 가능한 상태를 유지하는 점진적 순서를 권장 (예: Gradle 빌드 → 이벤트 루프/서버 → State/리스너 → 대기 → 스트림 → 서브프로세스 → 정리).
